questions.question: The average score of 22 players in an IPL match is 72. Out of these 22 players, the average score of 10 players is 80. the next 5 players got an average score of 75 and the rest 5 players got an average of 55. Then the average score of the remaining two players is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average score of 22 players in an IPL match is 72.

Out of these 22 players, the average score of 10 players is 80.

The next 5 players got an average score of 75.

The rest 5 players got an average score of 55.

**Formula Used:**

Average = Total Sum / Number of Players

Total Sum = Average × Number of Players

**Calculation:**

We have,

⇒ Total average score of 22 players = 72

⇒ Total sum of scores of 22 players = 72 × 22 = 1584

⇒ Average score of 10 players = 80

⇒ Total sum of scores of 10 players = 80 × 10 = 800

⇒ Average score of next 5 players = 75

⇒ Total sum of scores of next 5 players = 75 × 5 = 375

⇒ Average score of rest 5 players = 55

⇒ Total sum of scores of rest 5 players = 55 × 5 = 275

⇒ Sum of scores of 20 players = 800 + 375 + 275 = 1450

⇒ Sum of scores of remaining 2 players = Total sum - Sum of scores of 20 players

⇒ Sum of scores of remaining 2 players = 1584 - 1450 = 134

⇒ Average score of remaining 2 players = Sum of scores of remaining 2 players / 2

⇒ Average score of remaining 2 players = 134 / 2 = 67

**Hence, the average score of the remaining two players is 67.**

questions.question: The product of two numbers is 4107. If the HCF of these numbers is 37, then the greater number is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The product of two numbers is 4107. The HCF of these numbers is 37.

**Concept:**

If the product of two numbers is given and their HCF is known, then the product of the two numbers can be expressed as:

Product of numbers = (HCF) × (Product of the numbers when divided by HCF)

**Formula Used:**

Product of numbers = HCF × LCM

**Calculation:**

We have,

⇒ Product of two numbers = 4107

⇒ HCF of the numbers = 37

Let the numbers be 37a and 37b.

⇒ 37a × 37b = 4107

⇒ 37²ab = 4107

⇒ ab = 4107 / 37²

⇒ ab = 4107 / 1369

⇒ ab = 3

Since ab = 3 and the factors of 3 are 1 and 3, the possible pairs (a, b) are (1, 3) or (3, 1).

Therefore, the numbers are 37×1 and 37×3.

Hence, the greater number is:

⇒ 37 × 3 = 111

**∴ The greater number is 111.**

questions.question: Two places A and B are 60 km apart from each other on a highway. A car starts from A and another car from B at the same time. If they move in the same direction, they meet each other in 6 hours, If they move in the opposite direction towards each other, they meet in 1 hour 30 minutes. Find the speeds of the cars (in km/h).
questions.solution:
**Formula Used:**

When moving in the same direction, relative speed = |v₁ - v₂|

When moving in the opposite direction, relative speed = v₁ + v₂

Where v₁ and v₂ are the speeds of the two cars.

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of the car starting from A be v₁ km/h and the speed of the car starting from B be v₂ km/h.

**1. When moving in the same direction:**

⇒ Distance = Relative speed × Time

⇒ 60 km = |v₁ - v₂| × 6 hours

⇒ |v₁ - v₂| = 60 km / 6 hours

⇒ |v₁ - v₂| = 10 km/h ...(1)

**2. When moving in opposite directions:**

⇒ Distance = Relative speed × Time

⇒ 60 km = (v₁ + v₂) × 1.5 hours

⇒ v₁ + v₂ = 60 km / 1.5 hours

⇒ v₁ + v₂ = 40 km/h ...(2)

From equations (1) and (2):

⇒ v₁ - v₂ = 10 km/h ...(3)

⇒ v₁ + v₂ = 40 km/h ...(4)

Adding equations (3) and (4):

⇒ 2v₁ = 50 km/h

⇒ v₁ = 25 km/h

Substituting v₁ = 25 km/h into equation (4):

⇒ 25 + v₂ = 40

⇒ v₂ = 15 km/h

**∴ The speeds of the cars are 25 km/h and 15 km/h.**

A conical tent is set to accommodate 15 persons. Each person must have 5 square metres of space on the ground and 30 cubic metres of air to breathe.

**Concept:**

The volume and base area of a cone are given by the formulas:

Volume (V) = (1/3)πr²h

Base Area (A) = πr²

**Calculation:**

⇒ 15 persons × 5 m²/person = 75 m²

Total air required:

⇒ 15 persons × 30 m³/person = 450 m³

⇒ r² = 75/π

questions.question: By selling at a loss of 12% instead of a loss of 18% an article sells for Rs. 120 more. Find its CP.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

By selling at a loss of 12% instead of a loss of 18%, an article sells for Rs. 120 more.

**Concept:**

The difference in selling prices at different loss percentages can be used to find the cost price (CP) of the article.

**Formula Used:**

Let CP be the cost price.

Selling Price (SP) at 12% loss = CP × (1 - 12/100)

Selling Price (SP) at 18% loss = CP × (1 - 18/100)

Given that the difference in SP is Rs. 120.

**Calculation:**

We have,

⇒ CP × (1 - 12/100) - CP × (1 - 18/100) = 120

⇒ CP × (0.88) - CP × (0.82) = 120

⇒ CP × (0.88 - 0.82) = 120

⇒ CP × 0.06 = 120

⇒ CP = 120 / 0.06

⇒ CP = 2000

**∴ The cost price (CP) of the article is Rs. 2000.**

questions.question: A bank offers compound interest at the rate 5% per annum calculated half yearly on its deposits. A customer deposits Rs. 2,400 each on 1st January and 1st July of a year. Find the amount be received at the end of the year.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A bank offers compound interest at the rate of 5% per annum calculated half-yearly on its deposits. A customer deposits Rs. 2,400 each on 1st January and 1st July of a year.

**Concept:**

Compound Interest is calculated using the formula:

A = P(1 + r/n)ⁿt

Where:

 
• A = Amount
 
• P = Principal
 
• r = Annual interest rate (decimal)
 
• n = Number of times interest is compounded per year
 
• t = Time the money is invested for in years

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + r/n)ⁿt

**Calculation:**

For the deposit on 1st January:

⇒ P = Rs. 2,400, r = 5/100 = 0.05, n = 2, t = 1 year

⇒ A₁ = 2400(1 + 0.05/2)²×¹

⇒ A₁ = 2400(1 + 0.025)²

⇒ A₁ = 2400(1.025)²

⇒ A₁ = 2400 × 1.050625

⇒ A₁ ≈ Rs. 2521.50

For the deposit on 1st July:

⇒ P = Rs. 2,400, r = 0.05, n = 2, t = 0.5 years

⇒ A₂ = 2400(1 + 0.05/2)²×⁰.⁵

⇒ A₂ = 2400(1 + 0.025)¹

⇒ A₂ = 2400 × 1.025

⇒ A₂ ≈ Rs. 2460

Total Amount at the end of the year:

⇒ Total Amount = A₁ + A₂

⇒ Total Amount ≈ 2521.50 + 2460

⇒ Total Amount ≈ Rs. 4,981.50

**∴ The customer will receive Rs. 4,981.50 at the end of the year.**
